title: Attribute value is copied into terraform.tfstate as cleartext
msg: `{name}` on {block} is stored verbatim in terraform.tfstate. Terraform keeps no cleartext-attribute allowlist: every value it sends to the provider is written back to state. Move it to a secret manager and read it at apply time, or mark the whole path sensitive and encrypt state.

title: random_password writes the generated value into state
msg: `random_password.{label}` generates a secret and stores `result` in terraform.tfstate in cleartext forever — that is the documented behaviour of the random provider, not a bug. Anyone who can read the state file can read the password.

title: tls_private_key puts the PEM private key in state
msg: `tls_private_key.{label}` writes `private_key_pem` and `private_key_openssh` to terraform.tfstate. The hashicorp/tls provider documents this as unsuitable for production keys — generate the key outside Terraform and import only the public half.

title: Secret data source result is persisted in state
msg: `data.{type}.{label}` reads a live secret, and every data source result is persisted in terraform.tfstate. Reading a secret this way copies it out of the secret manager and into the state file on every plan.

title: Remote state bucket is written without server-side encryption
msg: The `backend "{type}"` block has no `encrypt = true` / `kms_key_id`, so the state object — including every cleartext value above — lands in object storage unencrypted.

title: terraform block has no state encryption
msg: Terraform 1.10 and later can encrypt state itself with a `terraform { encryption { ... } }` block, independent of where the backend stores it. This configuration has none, so plan files and state are written in cleartext by Terraform before the backend ever sees them.

title: Local backend keeps state as a plain file on disk
msg: `backend "local"` writes terraform.tfstate next to the code as an unencrypted JSON file. Add it to .gitignore and move to an encrypted remote backend before the first apply that touches a secret.

title: Output exposes a secret without sensitive = true
msg: `output "{label}"` returns a secret-bearing value but is not marked `sensitive = true`, so Terraform prints it to the console and to CI logs. Marking it sensitive hides the log line — it does not remove the value from state.

title: Secret-named variable is not marked sensitive
msg: `variable "{label}"` is named like a credential but has no `sensitive = true`, so its value appears in plan output and in the run log of any CI job.

title: Credential literal committed in the .tf file
msg: This line contains a {kind} written directly into the Terraform source, which puts it in git history as well as in state. Rotate it, then read it from a secret manager.
